senses.definition: A system that uses patterns of short and long signals to stand for letters, numbers and marks.
senses.example: The telegraph operator used Morse code to send the name of the town.

senses.definition: A set of equipment that joins selected telephone lines so callers can speak to each other.
senses.example: The operator used a cord at the telephone switchboard to connect two callers.

senses.definition: A dark space where light through a small opening makes a picture on a surface inside.
senses.example: A camera obscura showed an upside-down picture of the trees outside.

senses.definition: A stiff card whose holes in particular places stand for information.
senses.example: The machine used the holes on each punch card to add to a count.

senses.definition: A group of very small electronic parts built and connected on one piece of material.
senses.example: Many transistors can fit together in one integrated circuit.

senses.definition: A thin, flexible disk that stores information in magnetic patterns.
senses.example: He saved his school report on a floppy disk to take it to a different computer.
